name: rea
description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.
one_liner: Lets an AI assistant peek inside how any app actually works under the hood (even without its source code) and explain it, or rebuild the feature for you.
buyer: A software engineer or small product team who sees a slick feature in a competitor's app and wants to understand and replicate it, without hiring a dedicated reverse-engineering specialist.
business_use_cases: A solo app developer uses it to figure out how a competitor's onboarding flow or sync feature works, then builds a comparable feature for their own product.
A security consultant offers 'competitive feature teardown' reports to product teams, powered by this tool instead of manual binary analysis.
An agency building clones/alternatives of niche SaaS tools speeds up their build process by having the agent explain the original app's behavior first.

money_ideas.idea: Offer paid 'feature teardown' reports as a freelance service for product teams who want to understand a competitor's implementation.
Package it as part of a reverse-engineering-as-a-service retainer for app studios doing frequent competitive analysis.

steal_this: Pick one feature from a popular app you admire, run it through REA this weekend, and ship a blog post or demo rebuild — it's good marketing for a teardown-as-a-service offer.
